expectations_are: rule-derived predictions from manual trace of the design, not outputs of a run

cases.text: We found X and detected Y.
cases.note: Multiple result predicates via coordination: 'and' between them splits into two local assertions.

cases.text: We tested whether X predicted Y and found that X predicted Y.
cases.note: 'tested' is not in the mapper lexicon. Three raw hits (predicted, found, predicted): split at 'and', then merge the second 'predicted' into 'found' via 'that'.

cases.text: found X previous studies found Y
cases.note: Headless fragment, no punctuation at all: no that/and/or/but between the two 'found' hits. Genuinely undecidable -- both sides reported as ambiguous, neither silently merged nor split.

cases.text: We found X. We found X.
cases.note: Repeated target term across two separate sentences: trivially two independent local assertions, never compared against each other (sentence boundary already resolves it).

cases.text: Previous studies found X, but we found Y.
cases.note: A ', but' clause boundary already separates these into two clauses before the within-clause boundary logic ever runs, so each clause trivially has one match.

cases.text: Previous studies found X; we found Y.
cases.note: Semicolon clause boundary, same effect as the comma+contrast case.

cases.text: Previous studies found X, but we detected Y.
cases.note: Prior/current mixed passage, different predicate words, already separated by the clause boundary.

cases.text: The literature review associated X with Y.
cases.note: Review/background-prose wording; 'associated' is preserved and attached, admissibility undecided here.

cases.text: We did not find that scores increased.
cases.note: CORRECTED after the first run (a pure expectation bug, not a module bug): '_RESULT_PREDICATE' lists only the past-tense 'found', never the base form 'find' that correct do-support negation grammar requires ('did not find', never 'did not found'). So this sentence has exactly one raw hit, 'increased'; 'found' is never even a candidate. This is a genuine, concrete instance of the mapper lexicon disagreeing with assertion_authority's own _RESULT_VERBS (which lists found/find/finds all three) -- the module's logic is unaffected; this module has no concept of negation either way.

cases.text: We found no support for scores increasing.
cases.note: 'increasing' (present participle) is not in the mapper lexicon -- only 'increased'/'decreased' are -- so this is a single match on 'found' alone, with no embedded-content merge.

cases.text: Smith et al. observed that scores correlated with revenue.
cases.note: Citation-marked subject, same merge-via-'that' mechanics as mp_B; source is never inspected.

cases.text: We found X and detected Y and reported Z.
cases.note: Three coordinated result predicates in one clause split into three local assertions.
